competitors.title: AI Agent Runtime: The Execution Layer Behind Autonomous Systems
key_points: Agent runtime is the execution environment for production agents — manages session state, tool invocation, memory, and context windows
Core responsibilities: accept/validate requests, initialize sessions, execute logic, manage tools, persist state, handle streaming, record telemetry
Key differences from traditional backend: minutes-to-hours stateful vs milliseconds stateless, pause-resume vs crash-restart
Agent runtime ≠ agent framework: runtime is infrastructure (state, security, lifecycle), framework is reasoning logic
Three memory layers: session memory (current interaction), thread memory (across related sessions), long-term memory (KV + vector stores)
Scaling: horizontal with externalized state stores, resource isolation, multi-region deployment
Security: sandboxed code execution, centralized API key management, granular tool permissions, audit logging

angles: Context Window = RAM mental model: reframe agent failures as architecture problems, not model quality problems — most production failures stem from treating context windows as storage instead of working memory

Runtime vs Framework distinction: the agent runtime (infrastructure for state, security, lifecycle) is the constant; the agent framework (reasoning logic) is the variable — decouple them for production reliability

Three-layer persistence architecture: Orchestrate (workflow state machines), Remember (tiered memory with permissions), Verify (safety gates before privileged actions) — the scalable production pattern

Memory tiering strategy: session memory (ephemeral, current interaction) → thread memory (cross-session continuity) → long-term memory (KV + vector stores for persistent knowledge) — each with different durability and cost profiles

The 'idle-burst-idle' resource pattern: agent runtimes need session-based autoscaling (concurrent sessions + token throughput), not CPU-based — traditional infrastructure autoscaling fails for agent workloads

Pause-resume semantics: agents must suspend mid-session (waiting for human approval, external webhooks, long-running tools) and resume without losing accumulated context — traditional crash-restart models don't work

Security-first state persistence: sandboxed execution isolation, centralized API key management, granular tool permissions, Cedar policy language with default-deny — state increases capability and responsibility

The 2026 state persistence landscape: from AWS Bedrock Stateful Runtime (enterprise, OpenAI-powered) to open-source memory libraries (Mem0, Zep, Letta) to framework-agnostic runtimes (Agentuity) — choose by scale and governance needs
